subject: Request: short-term headroom + blended overage pricing for ScaleCraft pilot
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@scalecraft.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot spike — immediate uplift needed for next two weeks

Hi Olga,

Quick note from ScaleCraft: our pilot goes live tomorrow morning and we expect a concentrated spike in inference volume for ~10 business days. Baseline usage estimates are in the attached usage_report_Q2.csv, but short version: 6x token/s compared to our average.

Can Redwood provide a temporary headroom uplift and a short-term rate plan? Two priorities: (1) avoid 429s during the pilot window, and (2) keep unit economics reasonable — we can commit to a short 3-week committed top-up if that unlocks a mid-double-digit discount.

What do you need from us to move fast? PO? Signed addendum? Any lead time for capacity changes?

Thanks — Alice
Alice Moreno
Head of Platform Ops, ScaleCraft
alice@scalecraft.ai

Attachments: usage_report_Q2.csv (CSV summary of expected token volumes)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@scalecraft.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T11:05:33-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spike — immediate uplift needed for next two weeks

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up and the attachment.

Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary headroom uplift while keeping a blended pricing option for the short commitment. High-level proposal in this thread:
- Short-term uplift: 3x baseline headroom immediately, ramp to 5x within 24 hours if traffic materializes.
- Billing: two-part approach — (A) a time-boxed committed top-up (3-week minimum) with a 20% discount on the top-up portion; (B) pay-as-you-go overage beyond the top-up at a capped overrun rate. We can also apply a one-time credit if traffic estimated in the CSV proves materially lower.

I've attached a draft temporary_quota_addendum_draft.pdf that outlines terms and a simple SOW. To proceed quickly we need either (1) a signed addendum + PO, or (2) a written approval email from procurement confirming the billing contact and remit details.

Rafael — can you confirm capacity lead time and if the 5x ramp is safe? Ben — take a look at the proposed discount and invoicing cadence in the attached schedule and flag anything untenable.

Next steps: if ScaleCraft signs the addendum by EOD tomorrow, we can provision the initial uplift and monitor. I'll open a short-term guardrail policy so we can dial traffic shaping if needed.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0123

Attachments: temporary_quota_addendum_draft.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spike — capacity and traffic shaping notes

Olga — quick engineering note on capacity.

We can provision an immediate 3x uplift within ~2 hours of approval; moving to 5x requires a short warm-up period (KV cache priming and batch-slot redistribution), estimate 18–24 hours to reach steady-state with acceptable latency tail. We should also expect increased memory pressure on the serving fleet for long-context requests.

Operational suggestions:
- Open a temporary rate-limit profile tied to the ScaleCraft API key so we can track and surface any throttles.
- Enable prefix cache for frequent flows — that will materially reduce token compute and cost.
- If ScaleCraft can route heavy long-context requests to a separate inferencing route (lower parallelism), we can preserve p99 latency for interactive flows.

I attached a brief capacity_plan_2xbrief.txt with the steps. No infra blockers; just need a clear approval timestamp and the key to tag.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
SRE, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T14:20:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot spike — billing approach and discount options

All — notes on billing side.

We can do a 20% discount on the committed top-up volume for a 3-week closed window. Details:
- Commitment model: ScaleCraft prepays or provides a PO for the top-up amount (we can invoice upfront or net-30 depending on procurement).
- Discount applies only to the top-up tranche, not to baseline or overrun.
- Overrun beyond the top-up is billed PAYG at a capped premium of +15% over standard PAYG rates (this cap is time-boxed to the 3-week window).
- We'll include a reconciliation line on the month-end invoice if actual consumption is materially below the commit (we can apply credit or refund per the addendum).

I've attached a proposed_invoice_schedule.xlsx that outlines invoice timing and expected line items. If procurement wants Net-45, we can route through enterprise billing but that will delay provisioning until we have contractual approval.

Happy to sync with procurement if they want to discuss payment terms.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Alice — looping back with the agreed path and next actions so procurement has a single-step checklist.

Agreed path:
1) Provisioning: we will enable a 3x uplift immediately upon receipt of your signed addendum or PO. If we see sustained traffic we will ramp to 5x within ~24 hours. Rafael will manage the warm-up and prefix-caching.
2) Billing: ScaleCraft will commit to a 3-week top-up tranche with a 20% discount on that tranche. Overruns billed PAYG with a capped premium (+15%) for the window. Monthly reconciliation will apply per the addendum.
3) Approvals needed: signed temporary_quota_addendum_draft.pdf OR Procurement written approval email; billing contact for invoicing; PO number if preferring prepay.
4) DocuSign link (for convenience): https://redwood.app/docusign/abc123

If procurement can send a signed addendum by EOD tomorrow we will provision the initial uplift and stand up the rate-limit profile. I'll follow up with a short status note once Rafael confirms the ramp.

Thanks — excited to see ScaleCraft's pilot go live.

—Olga
